newsitem.title: USA: Florida police holding serial killer suspect.
newsitem.headline: Florida police holding serial killer suspect.

text.p: Florida police said Friday they were holding a 61-year-old suspected serial killer in custody, calling him the prime suspect in seven murders stretching back to 1983.
William Darrell Lindsey, a former resident of St. Augustine, was arrested Dec. 27 in Ashville, N.C., and charged with murder there.
Lindsey then became a suspect in January in a series of murders in Florida's St. Johns County, St. Johns Sheriff Neil J. Perry said.
"Some former residents of St. Johns County ... sent me a newspaper article about Lindsey's arrest," Perry said Friday.
Noting that Perry had lived in St. Augustine, he dispatched detectives to North Carolina to interview Lindsey.

Those interviews showed Lindsey had direct knowledge of the seven unsolved murders of Lisa Foley, 24; Anita Stevens, 27; Constance Terrell, 26; Lashawna Streeter, 27; Donetha Snead-Haile, 32; Cheryl Lucas, 31; and Diana Richardson, 48, Perry said.
The murders began in 1983 and continued until 1995.
Sheriffs brought Lindsey back to Florida Monday, Perry said. Meanwhile, scuba divers were searching a pit where Lindsey told detectives he dumped one of the bodies in 1993.

Perry said there is no rush to charge Lindsey with the murders since he is already being held on the murder charge in North Carolina. The State Attorneys Office in St. Johns County probably will present evidence to a grand jury when the investigations are complete, Perry said.
